answer:
All hashes verified against alloc8or's nativedb data (natives.json, updated 2026-07-16 to current builds); wrappers verified in SHVDN source (v3.6.0 stable tag and current main/nightly). Full signatures in facts.

(1) TASK_VEHICLE_DRIVE_TO_COORD_LONGRANGE (speed, driveMode, stopRange) — SHVDN Ped.Task.DriveTo. Short-range: TASK_VEHICLE_DRIVE_TO_COORD. Mid-task tweaks: SET_DRIVE_TASK_DRIVING_STYLE, SET_DRIVE_TASK_CRUISE_SPEED.
(2) Documented bits (FiveM eVehicleDrivingFlags = SHVDN VehicleDrivingFlags): 1 StopForVehicles, 2 StopForPeds, 4 SwerveAroundAllVehicles, 8 SteerAroundStationaryVehicles, 16 SteerAroundPeds, 32 SteerAroundObjects, 64 DontSteerAroundPlayerPed, 128 StopAtTrafficLights, 256 GoOffRoadWhenAvoiding, 512 AllowGoingWrongWay, 1024 Reverse, 262144 UseShortCutLinks, 524288 ChangeLanesAroundObstructions, 2097152 UseSwitchedOffNodes, 4194304 PreferNavmeshRoute, 16777216 ForceStraightLine, 1073741824 ForceJoinInRoadDirection, 2147483648 StopAtDestination (rest in facts). Combos: normal=786603; ignore-lights=786475 (FiveM) or 2883621 (SHVDN DrivingStyle.IgnoreLights); rushed=1074528293; avoid-traffic=786468/786469; extreme=6.
(3) TASK_FOLLOW_NAV_MESH_TO_COORD / TASK_GO_STRAIGHT_TO_COORD — Ped.Task.GoTo/RunTo (stable); FollowNavMeshTo/GoStraightTo (nightly).
(4) TASK_ENTER_VEHICLE — Ped.Task.EnterVehicle; nearest: GET_CLOSEST_VEHICLE (World.GetClosestVehicle) + EnterVehicle, or Ped.Task.EnterAnyVehicle.
(5) TASK_VEHICLE_DRIVE_WANDER — Ped.Task.CruiseWithVehicle.
(6) TASK_SMART_FLEE_PED/COORD — Ped.Task.FleeFrom; TASK_COMBAT_HATED_TARGETS_AROUND_PED/_IN_AREA — FightAgainstHatedTargets (stable) / CombatHatedTargetsAroundPed (nightly); TASK_SEEK_COVER_FROM_PED/_FROM_POS — no wrapper (raw Function.Call); TASK_FOLLOW_TO_OFFSET_OF_ENTITY — FollowToOffsetFromEntity.
(7) SET_TIME_SCALE — Game.TimeScale (0.0–1.0).
(8) GET_MISSION_FLAG — Game.IsMissionActive; also GET_RANDOM_EVENT_FLAG — Game.IsRandomEventActive.
(9) IS_CUTSCENE_ACTIVE — Game.IsCutsceneActive; IS_CUTSCENE_PLAYING (no wrapper).
(10) SET_PLAYER_CONTROL — Player.CanControlCharacter; read state: IS_PLAYER_CONTROL_ON.
(11) NETWORK_IS_SESSION_STARTED (also NETWORK_IS_IN_SESSION, NETWORK_IS_GAME_IN_PROGRESS, NETWORK_IS_SESSION_ACTIVE) — no SHVDN wrapper.
(12) Pure reads: GET_PLAYER_WANTED_LEVEL — Player.WantedLevel getter (stable) / Player.Wanted.WantedLevel (nightly); GET_MAX_WANTED_LEVEL.
(13) GET_STREET_NAME_AT_COORD + GET_STREET_NAME_FROM_HASH_KEY — World.GetStreetName; GET_NAME_OF_ZONE — World.GetZoneDisplayName; localized via GET_FILENAME_FOR_AUDIO_CONVERSATION (World.GetZoneLocalizedName).
(14) GET_CLOCK_HOURS/MINUTES/SECONDS — World.CurrentTimeOfDay (stable) / GTA.Chrono.GameClock (nightly); GET_PREV/NEXT_WEATHER_TYPE_HASH_NAME — World.Weather/.NextWeather.
(15) SET_RADIO_TO_STATION_NAME / SET_VEH_RADIO_STATION / SET_RADIO_TO_STATION_INDEX — Game.RadioStation (get/set), Vehicle.RadioStation (set-only).
(16) START_VEHICLE_HORN — Vehicle.SoundHorn(ms).
(17) IS_ENTITY_UPSIDEDOWN — Entity.IsUpsideDown; IS_ENTITY_IN_WATER — Entity.IsInWater; GET_ENTITY_SUBMERGED_LEVEL — Entity.SubmersionLevel.
(18) Enumerate GET_FIRST/NEXT_BLIP_INFO_ID (argument is a blip sprite id) + DOES_BLIP_EXIST; coords GET_BLIP_INFO_ID_COORD; identify via GET_BLIP_SPRITE/GET_BLIP_COLOUR/GET_BLIP_INFO_ID_TYPE. SHVDN: World.GetAllBlips/GetNearbyBlips (memory scan), Blip.Position/.Sprite/.Color/.ShowRoute. "Mission objective = Standard sprite (1) + Yellow colour (66) + route" is empirical convention, not documented.
(19) IS_PLAYER_DEAD — Player.IsDead; IS_PLAYER_BEING_ARRESTED (no wrapper); IS_PED_DEAD_OR_DYING; IS_PLAYER_PLAYING covers dead/injured/arrested.
Legacy/Enhanced: same hashes, one shared DB; official SHVDN targets Legacy (nightly ≥3.6.0-nightly.89 required on game b3258+); Enhanced needs the ScriptHookVDotNetEnhanced fork plus Enhanced ScriptHookV.

facts.claim: alloc8or gta5-nativedb-data last commit 2026-07-16 'update to 3889.0/1158.13' — the DB used for all hashes above is current as of July 2026 and contains no per-native Legacy/Enhanced (gen9) annotations (zero matches for 'gen9'/'enhanced' in natives.json)

Official SHVDN README: latest stable GitHub release is v3.6.0 (2022-12-29); on game v1.0.3258.0+ users must run nightly v3.6.0-nightly.89 or later (v3.6.0/v3.5.1 have a compatibility issue with b3258+); devs are told to build against stable API, nightly-only APIs may break

ScriptHookVDotNetEnhanced (Chiheb-Bacha fork, last pushed 2026-07-15) is 'an extended version of ScriptHookVDotNet to support both GTA5 Legacy and Enhanced'; scripts built for Legacy run as-is unless they rely on their own memory patterns

gotchas: Hash drift in old tutorials: current DB hashes differ from many older forum pastes (e.g. GET_PLAYER_WANTED_LEVEL is 0xE28E54788CE8F12D, SET_PLAYER_WANTED_LEVEL is 0x39FF19C64EF7DA5B, SET_RADIO_TO_STATION_NAME is 0xC69EDA28699D5107, IS_CUTSCENE_ACTIVE is 0x991251AFC3981F84). Use SHVDN's GTA.Native.Hash enum or the July-2026 natives.json, not copy-pasted constants from 2015-era posts.

Sources disagree on the named 'ignore lights'/'rushed' combos: SHVDN's legacy DrivingStyle enum uses IgnoreLights=2883621 (= 786469 + UseSwitchedOffNodes 2097152) and Rushed=1074528293 (= 786469 + ForceJoinInRoadDirection 1073741824), while FiveM's documented modes are DrivingModeStopForVehiclesIgnoreLights=786475 and DrivingModeAvoidVehicles(Reckless)=786469/786468. The individual bits are documented; which combo to call 'rushed' is convention from the gtaforums 'Guide: Driving Styles' thread (empirical).

SHVDN API churn between stable v3.6.0 and nightly/main: DriveTo argument order changed ((veh, target, radius, speed, DrivingStyle) -> (veh, target, speed, VehicleDrivingFlags, radius)); GoTo(Vector3) -> FollowNavMeshTo; FightAgainstHatedTargets -> CombatHatedTargetsAroundPed; Player.WantedLevel -> Player.Wanted.WantedLevel; World.CurrentTimeOfDay -> GTA.Chrono.GameClock; Player.CanControlCharacter setter is obsoleted. Pin your SHVDN version and compile against it.

GET_FIRST/GET_NEXT_BLIP_INFO_ID iterate per blip SPRITE id, so enumerating 'all blips' via natives means looping over sprite ids; SHVDN World.GetAllBlips instead does an internal memory scan (GetNonCriticalRadarBlipHandles) — convenient, but memory-pattern-dependent, which is exactly the part the Enhanced fork warns about.

There is no native to READ a blip's route flag (SET_BLIP_ROUTE is set-only); SHVDN Blip.ShowRoute's getter is a raw memory-flag read. Identifying the story-mission objective blip as 'sprite Standard(1) + colour Yellow(66) + route enabled' is empirical community practice, not documented by any primary source — validate in-game per mission.

SET_MISSION_FLAG can only set the flag true (calling with false does nothing per the DB comment) and blocks saving; random events (Strangers & Freaks style ambient content) use GET_RANDOM_EVENT_FLAG instead of GET_MISSION_FLAG, so check both for 'is scripted content active'.

IS_PLAYER_BEING_ARRESTED(player, TRUE) returns true early (hands-up phase, player still has control); with FALSE it only returns true once actually busted. IS_PLAYER_PLAYING is a useful single check (false when dead/injured/arrested). TASK_COMBAT_HATED_TARGETS_* despite the plural name attacks only the single closest hated target, and requires relationship (hate/dislike/neutral) setup or the task exits immediately.

Legacy vs Enhanced: native names/hashes are shared (one alloc8or DB covers both, updated for 2026 builds of each), but tooling differs — official ScriptHookVDotNet targets Legacy (and needs nightly >= v3.6.0-nightly.89 on b3258+), while Enhanced requires the ScriptHookVDotNetEnhanced fork plus the Enhanced build of ScriptHookV. SHVDN features that bypass natives via memory patterns (GetAllBlips, Blip.ShowRoute getter, Game.TimeScale getter) are the risk area on Enhanced.
SET_TIME_SCALE only accepts 0.0-1.0 (cannot speed the game up), persists until changed, and at 0.0 the game still runs at a minimum time scale.
GET_CLOSEST_VEHICLE's flags parameter is only partially documented ('bitwise flags, commonly 70/71'); test empirically or use SHVDN World.GetClosestVehicle which hides it.
unconfirmed: Whether any of the ~60 listed natives behaves differently (or is stubbed) in GTA V Enhanced vs Legacy: the alloc8or DB carries no per-edition annotations and I found no primary source documenting per-native Enhanced differences for these specific natives — treat as identical but verify on the Enhanced target if you switch editions.

Exact semantic difference between IS_CUTSCENE_ACTIVE and IS_CUTSCENE_PLAYING (commonly: ACTIVE becomes true once a cutscene is requested/loaded, PLAYING only while actually playing) — no comment in the native DB; community/empirical only.

The claim that ScriptHookV itself disables all custom scripts when a GTA Online session is active (dev-c.com's stated policy) — widely reported but I did not re-verify dev-c.com today; NETWORK_IS_SESSION_STARTED remains the correct in-script guard regardless.

Nightly SHVDN version labels seen in the wild (e.g. 'v3.7.0-nightly') — the official repo's nightly release repo exists (scripthookvdotnet-nightly), but I did not verify current nightly version numbers; third-party mirrors (libertycity, gta5-mods) are not primary sources.
Units of the speed parameter in TASK_VEHICLE_DRIVE_TO_COORD_LONGRANGE / TASK_VEHICLE_DRIVE_WANDER (commonly treated as meters/second) — not stated in the native DB.
Full meaning of GET_CLOSEST_VEHICLE's flags bitfield (DB comment is truncated/incomplete; '70' is the commonly used value).

BlipColor 66 = the yellow used by story-mission objective blips: SHVDN's enum documents 66 as Yellow, but the mapping 'story objective blip is always colour 66 + sprite 1' is empirical, and some missions use sprite-specific blips (character sprites for M/F/T) instead.
